children.name: Article Lead
children.text: Drain nodes and upgrade Kubernetes without corrupting worlds, stranding volumes, or exceeding supported disruption limits.

children.name: Article Callout Text
children.text: Portability depends on storage topology, GPU and port constraints, affinity, and real spare capacity—not just a Ready destination node.

children.name: Section Body 1
children.text: Confirm compatibility, capacity, workload placement, storage mobility, maintenance communication, and recent backups.

children.name: Section 1 Item Text 0
children.text: Check Kubernetes, CSI, ingress, cert-manager, and rollback support.

children.name: Section 1 Item Text 1
children.text: Inventory affected servers; announce, save worlds, and verify backups.

children.name: Section 1 Item Text 2
children.text: Identify local volumes, GPUs, NodePorts, affinity, and non-movable pods.

children.name: Section Body 2
children.text: Move one failure domain at a time using deliberate eviction behavior and provider-supported ordering.

children.name: Section 2 Item Text 0
children.text: Cordon, then stop or migrate servers according to storage behavior.

children.name: Section 2 Item Text 1
children.text: Drain with explicit flags/timeouts; never force-delete state blindly.

children.name: Section 2 Item Text 2
children.text: Observe API, operator, agent, CSI, and ingress health during upgrade.

children.name: Section Body 3
children.text: Uncordon only after node, runtime, network, CSI, certs, and capacity are healthy, then validate every affected workflow.

children.name: Quick Reference Line 1
children.text: 01  Compatibility + capacity + movable storage + backups gate

children.name: Quick Reference Line 2
children.text: 02  Cordon → save/stop/migrate → drain → upgrade → health check

children.name: Quick Reference Line 3
children.text: 03  Uncordon → validate pods, PVCs, endpoints, backups, alerts, audit
